title: A clear type scale and a spacing rhythm
note: Headings, body and captions step clearly in size; spacing comes from one scale, not from guesses.
intent: A page looks designed when its sizes and gaps repeat. Pick a type scale (for example 12, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40 px) and use only those; body text 16 px at 1.5 line height in a column no wider than about 72 characters; headings clearly larger and heavier than body; captions smaller and muted. Take every gap from a spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 px) kept as CSS variables, and make like things look alike: one corner radius, one border colour, one button height. Never separate blocks with nothing: margins between sections should be larger than margins within them.

check.ask: Do headings, body text and captions step clearly in size, and is the spacing between and within blocks consistent?
check.note: A clear type hierarchy and consistent spacing are visible.

port: The owner of styles.css defines the scales as custom properties; facets use var(--space-3) and var(--text-lg), never raw numbers.
